title: Release checks and rollback awareness
learningObjectives: Explain release checks and rollback awareness and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: Release readiness includes validated builds, automated checks, security review, smoke tests, environment configuration, monitoring, backup or recovery plans, and a rollback strategy. A rollback returns users to a known-good release when the new version causes unacceptable issues.
understand.whyItMatters: A release is a controlled operational change. Rollback reduces the time users remain exposed to a broken deployment, but data migrations may require a separate forward-fix plan.
understand.analogy: A release is opening a new route to users while keeping a safe route back if the change fails.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The object models a gate with pending checks. It is not a release approval until every required condition is satisfied.

examples.explanation: The object models a gate with pending checks. It is not a release approval until every required condition is satisfied.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Write a release checklist with go/no-go criteria and a rollback plan. Include how to handle irreversible data migrations.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.

options: To restore a known-good release when a deployment fails
questions.answer: To restore a known-good release when a deployment fails
questions.explanation: Rollback reduces user impact by returning to a stable version where feasible.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable engineering workflow?
options: Inspect, validate, document, and verify changes
Assume a successful command means the whole release is healthy
questions.answer: Inspect, validate, document, and verify changes
questions.explanation: Reliable workflows use evidence and plan for failure rather than relying on assumptions.
